samples.summary: The runner's new `drag` action branch is never executed by any test — the "positive control" bypasses it
samples.evidence: `runAction`'s `case "drag"` (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:296-307) does three things: `resolveTarget(action.target)`, `resolveTarget(action.to)`, and the `at()` reduction of a role locator to its `boundingBox()` centre. The only end-to-end exercise added, `checkSlidesDrag` in verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:663-757, calls `performDrag(page, a.value, b.value)` directly with points it read itself — it never builds a `{type:"drag", target, to}` action and never goes through `runAction`. So the shared module proves only the mouse sequence, not the action: `to` resolution, the point/locator branch, and the `boundingBox()`-may-be-null path (`b.x` on null throws) are wholly untested. The header comment in hunt-ui-gesture.mjs claiming the lane exercises the same dispatch as the driver overstates what is shared.

samples.summary: checkSlidesDrag and the new bridge readers are only covered by a script no CI lane runs
samples.evidence: `verify-hunt-oracles.mjs` is wired as `pnpm verify:hunt:oracles` -> `frontend test:hunt-oracles` (package.json:16, packages/frontend/package.json:21), but grepping `hunt` in scripts/verify-ci.mjs, scripts/verify-self.mjs and all of .github/ returns no matches, and CI runs `pnpm verify:self` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:229). So the exact-coordinate drag assertions and every assertion about `slides.pointAt` / `slides.handleCenter` are manual-only; the sole mechanically-enforced coverage of this change is the plan-shape test in scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs. A regression in the readers or the drag geometry would go green.

samples.summary: No test covers `drag`'s `to` as a cross-surface reader door — and checkSurfaceScope does not inspect it
samples.evidence: hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:169 ("checkSurfaceScope covers wait, click targets and predictions, not just read") enumerates every reader-bearing field a caller can use to reach another surface. `drag` adds a fourth: `action.to.reader`. `checkSurfaceScope` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187) still cites only `action.reader`, `action.target.reader` and `action.expect.read`, so `{type:"drag", target:{role:...}, to:{reader:"sheet.cellCenter"}}` passes the surface pin, and no test in the new diff asserts otherwise. The missing test is exactly what let the missing case ship.

samples.summary: The new `asNumber` guard (NaN / non-number coordinates) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `asNumber` (bridge.ts:192-201) is new validation whose stated purpose is refusing NaN and non-numbers for `slides.pointAt`. No frontend test file exists for bridge.ts (glob of packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/** shows only slides-seed.test.ts), and verify-hunt-oracles.mjs only exercises `slides.pointAt(960,540)` and the off-slide refusal `(5000,100)` — never `NaN`, `"960"`, `undefined` or a missing second argument. The guard could be deleted and everything would still pass.

samples.summary: Two of `slides.handleCenter`'s three refusal branches are unexercised
samples.evidence: verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:748-754 asserts only the no-selection refusal (`/Nothing is selected/`). The branch that lists `Available: ...` when something IS selected but the kind is unknown (bridge.ts:588-596), and the off-slide refusal for a handle outside the canvas (bridge.ts:600-606), have no assertion anywhere — the off-slide message could be wrong or the branch inverted and nothing would notice.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. hunt-ui-runner.mjs:296-307 contains a new `case "drag"` that resolves `action.target` and `action.to` and reduces a role locator through `locator.boundingBox()` (unguarded). No test anywhere executes it: (a) checkSlidesDrag (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:667-758, helper at 678-685) calls performDrag directly with reader points it read itself, never constructing a `{type:"drag"}` action, so it never enters runAction and never takes the locator branch; (b) the only drag-shaped objects in the repo are in the plan validator and its unit test (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:44,154; hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs:96-127), which assert only assertSafeActionPlan; (c) both lanes that run the real runner use non-drag actions — FUNNEL_PLAN via runUiPlan is goto/read/type/type (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:1374-1391,1415) and the serve-mode control sends goto/type/read (1459-1490); (d) hunt-ui-session.test.mjs drives a stub runner with read/click only, and hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs:357-378 writes a stub runner. performDrag/DRAG_STEPS (hunt-ui-gesture.mjs:20,29) have only two importers, the runner and the verify script, so no unit test drives the gesture with a fake page either. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed behavior (the drag dispatch: `to` resolution, point-vs-locator branch, null boundingBox) shipped with a control that bypasses the code under test — major, and the gesture-only coverage does not close it.

finding.evidence: `verify-hunt-oracles.mjs` is wired as `pnpm verify:hunt:oracles` -> `frontend test:hunt-oracles` (package.json:16, packages/frontend/package.json:21), but grepping `hunt` in scripts/verify-ci.mjs, scripts/verify-self.mjs and all of .github/ returns no matches, and CI runs `pnpm verify:self` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:229). So the exact-coordinate drag assertions and every assertion about `slides.pointAt` / `slides.handleCenter` are manual-only; the sole mechanically-enforced coverage of this change is the plan-shape test in scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs. verdict.reason: A CI lane does run verify-hunt-oracles.mjs; the wiring is indirect, so greps for "hunt" in .github/ and in verify-self/verify-ci could not find it. Chain: ci.yml:290 defines the required verify-browser job, whose step at ci.yml:384-391 runs `docker run ... wafflebase-playwright` with WAFFLEBASE_DOCKER_BROWSER=true; Dockerfile.playwright:7 sets that image's CMD to `node ./scripts/verify-browser-lanes.mjs`; scripts/verify-browser-lanes.mjs:72 unconditionally execSyncs `pnpm verify:hunt:oracles` (comment at lines 68-71 says it lives there instead of verify:self because it needs Chromium; the Playwright early-exit at line 29 is bypassed when isDocker). That resolves via package.json:16 and packages/frontend/package.json:21 to verify-hunt-oracles.mjs, where checkSlidesDrag is invoked unconditionally in the main flow (line 1617), problems accumulate into failures, and the script exits 1 on failures (lines 1683-1687). So the exact-coordinate drag assertion (line 703) and the slides.pointAt / slides.handleCenter refusal assertions (lines 747-756) are mechanically enforced by a required check, not manual-only. The job is step-gated rather than job-gated (ci.yml:293-324) and RUN_HEAVY (ci.yml:338-341) is true whenever any workspace package changed, which includes packages/frontend where this change lives; scripts/verify-ci.mjs:16 runs the same wrapper as `verify:browser`.

finding.summary: No test covers `drag`'s `to` as a cross-surface reader door — and checkSurfaceScope does not inspect it
finding.evidence: hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:169 ("checkSurfaceScope covers wait, click targets and predictions, not just read") enumerates every reader-bearing field a caller can use to reach another surface. `drag` adds a fourth: `action.to.reader`. `checkSurfaceScope` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187) still cites only `action.reader`, `action.target.reader` and `action.expect.read`, so `{type:"drag", target:{role:...}, to:{reader:"sheet.cellCenter"}}` passes the surface pin, and no test in the new diff asserts otherwise. The missing test is exactly what let the missing case ship.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `checkSurfaceScope` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187) builds its `cited` list from only `action.reader`, `action.target.reader` and `action.expect.read`; `action.to` — the reader-bearing destination newly accepted for `drag` (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:154-163, hunt-ui-tool.mjs:565, runner at hunt-ui-runner.mjs:296-307) — is never inspected. The enumerating test at hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:169-181 covers exactly the three fields the code covers (wait reader, click target.reader, expect.read) and no drag case; its comment at :167 still says "three separate doors". The only drag tests anywhere (hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs:96-127) pin shape and namespace PREFIX via assertReader (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:77-82), which accepts `sheet.cellCenter` on a slides run — a different invariant, so it is not coverage of the surface pin. Repo-wide greps for `to.reader`, `type: "drag"`, `checkSurfaceScope`, `surface-scope` and `readersForSurface` turned up no test asserting a cross-surface reader in a drag's `to` is refused, and the runner resolves `to` through the same unscoped `resolveTarget`, so there is no indirect coverage downstream either. In-lane and major: a newly added reader-bearing field on a security-relevant guard whose three sibling fields each have an explicit test, while the new one has none — the untested door is precisely the gap that shipped.
